CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: MEDIUM: dynamic reload and reconciliation are established production patterns, but coupling generation fencing, atomic publication, runtime-state migration, draining, restart checkpointing, and telemetry garbage collection into one causal state-transition system gives the candidate a materially more distinctive shape than a generic reload task.
EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: bursts of watcher or discovery events
invalid updates mixed with valid endpoint changes
backend disappearance during an active request
stale affinity targeting an ineligible backend
restart during or immediately after an update
rapid remove and re-add of the same endpoint
concurrent request readers racing with state publication
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Implement generation-safe dynamic route and upstream reconciliation so configuration and backend-membership changes can be applied atomically under concurrent traffic, rolling backend turnover, invalid updates, and process restart.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: Only the solver-visible target is assumed: a Go public-facing HTTP edge-routing and traffic-management runtime. No hidden incident history, pre-existing topology, private design, implementation defect, oracle behavior, or verifier-private expectation is assumed.
CANDIDATES.INSTRUCTION_FIT: The material behavior can be expressed in roughly 10-12 concise family-level requirements, remaining comfortably within the strict instruction-size limit without exposing an implementation blueprint.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Rebuilding all load-balancing or sticky state on every reload makes an apparently correct reload path operationally unstable.
Publishing routes before their referenced pools produces mixed-generation request handling.
Validating syntax without generation fencing still permits stale updates to win races.
Removing a backend immediately can terminate or strand in-flight traffic.
Keeping retired endpoint metrics indefinitely creates stale observations and unbounded cardinality.
Checkpointing metadata before the complete runtime generation is durable can recover a state that was never safely published.
Treating duplicate endpoint aliases as independent identities can split health and load-balancing state.
CANDIDATES.PERSONA: Edge platform engineer or SRE responsible for a public-facing Go HTTP edge-routing runtime.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: In-flight and long-lived requests remain valid across unrelated updates.
Unchanged route semantics remain stable across generations.
Healthy unchanged endpoints preserve meaningful runtime selection and affinity state.
A rejected update cannot damage the currently serving generation.
Readers never observe a partially applied configuration.
Runtime and observability state remain bounded after repeated updates.
REASONING_CHAIN: diff the endpoint and route graph
serve requests through health, selection, retry, stickiness, and drain state
retire unreachable runtime objects and telemetry
recover a complete last-known-good generation after restart
REQUIRED_END_STATE: Configuration inputs are validated and compiled into immutable runtime snapshots before publication.
Every accepted configuration generation is fenced so stale or out-of-order generations cannot overwrite newer state.
Route and upstream-pool state becomes visible atomically rather than through partially applied generations.
Endpoint reconciliation identifies additions, removals, and unchanged endpoints using stable runtime identity.
Reusable load-balancing, stickiness, health, and lifecycle state is preserved for unchanged endpoints.
Removed endpoints enter an explicit draining lifecycle before retirement instead of disappearing immediately.
Retries and sticky routing avoid endpoints that are no longer eligible while preserving continuity where safe.
Invalid updates leave the last-known-good generation serving traffic.
The latest accepted generation can be checkpointed and recovered without publishing mixed or partially restored state.
Lifecycle telemetry and per-generation or per-endpoint metrics are garbage-collected when their owning runtime state is retired.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: weighted, sticky, retry, and failover selection
observability lifecycle and metric garbage collection

SCALE_FIT.SUBSTANTIVE_RUNTIME_LOC: Naturally supports at least 3000 substantive reachable runtime/configuration LOC without filler.

CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: MEDIUM_HIGH: health-aware load balancing is a common benchmark shape. The lifecycle-state-machine treatment makes it credible but less original than the recommended candidate.
EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: health request affected by routing middleware
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Build a coherent health-aware upstream-pool state machine combining active and passive health signals with weighted selection, stickiness, retries, failover, dynamic membership, and safe all-down behavior.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: Only the solver-visible Go edge-routing runtime target is assumed. No excluded implementation, incident, oracle, review, or verifier state is treated as inherited fact.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: A probe can report false failures if its TLS name, host, or transport differs from normal traffic.
Retries can repeatedly select the same failed endpoint.
Passive failure counters can permanently poison an endpoint if they never decay.
Affinity can continue pinning clients to an unhealthy endpoint.
Parent failover state can disagree with the health of nested child services.
Reloading can silently reset health state and cause traffic oscillation.
Duplicate endpoint representations can be counted as independent capacity.
CANDIDATES.PERSONA: Traffic reliability engineer responsible for upstream selection and failure containment in a Go edge service.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: Healthy-peer traffic distribution remains meaningful.
Sticky clients remain on their healthy target when possible.
Retry behavior cannot create uncontrolled amplification.
Health probing remains bounded under large pools.
Existing request semantics remain unchanged when all upstreams are healthy.
REASONING_CHAIN: retry or fail over when permitted
REQUIRED_END_STATE: Active probes use the correct upstream transport, host, scheme, timeout, and TLS identity.
Passive request failures update bounded health state with explicit aging or decay.
Health transitions use deterministic state rules rather than instantaneous uncontrolled flapping.
Only eligible endpoints participate in load balancing.
Retries exclude already failed or newly ineligible targets.
Sticky affinity is retained for healthy endpoints and safely remapped when its target becomes unavailable.
Composite failover or weighted services propagate child health correctly.
Dynamic endpoint additions and removals reconcile without leaking health state.
The zero-healthy-endpoint case fails deterministically without retry amplification.
Probe, endpoint, and transition telemetry remains bounded.

SCALE_FIT.F2P_SURFACE: Approximately 25-30 distinct behavioral tests are credible.
SCALE_FIT.P2P_SURFACE: Good preservation coverage exists for healthy routing, affinity, weighting, and bounded probes.
SCALE_FIT.RISK: The scope can degrade into a feature collection unless all requirements are organized around a single endpoint-health state machine.
SCALE_FIT.SUBSTANTIVE_RUNTIME_LOC: Approximately 3000-5000 substantive LOC is plausible when implemented as one health and pool lifecycle system.

CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: HIGH: protocol-safe reverse-proxy hardening is an established task family and is less differentiated despite offering good technical depth.
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Harden the complete HTTP proxy request and response pipeline across route rewriting, forwarding trust, query handling, transport/TLS, streaming, upgrades, cancellation, retries, and error mapping.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: Only the solver-visible Go HTTP edge-runtime target is inherited; no private defect list or current implementation behavior is presumed.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Forwarded-header reconstruction can accidentally preserve spoofed client values.
Query normalization can change malformed or deliberately escaped inputs.
Path rewriting can double-escape segments.
A retry can silently replay a non-replayable request body incorrectly.
Streaming or upgrade paths can leak goroutines or connections.
A single broad timeout can break long-lived streams.
Host and TLS SNI can disagree.
CANDIDATES.PERSONA: Go networking engineer responsible for correctness and trust boundaries in a public HTTP edge runtime.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: Standards-compatible forwarding behavior
byte-safe path and query semantics
streaming latency
request-body integrity
client cancellation propagation
normal successful proxy behavior
REASONING_CHAIN: relay normal, streaming, or upgraded response
REQUIRED_END_STATE: Path and query rewriting preserves intended byte and escaping semantics.
Untrusted forwarding metadata is removed or reconstructed according to an explicit trust boundary.
Hop-by-hop request and response headers are handled correctly.
Upstream Host and TLS server-name behavior is deterministic.
Streaming responses and flush behavior remain low-latency.
Protocol upgrades have explicit lifecycle and cancellation handling.
Client cancellation propagates upstream.
Timeouts distinguish appropriate request phases.
Retries occur only when request bodies and methods are safely replayable.
Transport and response failures map to deterministic downstream behavior and telemetry.

SCALE_FIT.DEFECT_MANIFESTATIONS: Approximately 20 materially distinct manifestations are plausible.
SCALE_FIT.P2P_SURFACE: Strong preservation surface for ordinary proxying and streaming.
SCALE_FIT.SUBSTANTIVE_RUNTIME_LOC: Can reach the 3000 LOC strict floor naturally but has less structural breadth than the recommended reconciliation candidate.

CANDIDATES.DUPLICATE_RISK: MEDIUM: graceful backend turnover is a familiar operational concern, but a full explicit lifecycle with affinity, retry, transport disposal, and state garbage collection remains a coherent production-sized package.
EDGE_FAILURE_SURFACE: backend disappears before graceful drain completes
rolling membership changes with affinity enabled
CANDIDATES.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Implement an explicit backend lifecycle from discovery through readiness, active service, draining, and retirement so rolling membership changes do not create avoidable routing failures or leaked runtime state.
CANDIDATES.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: The only inherited fact is the solver-visible Go edge-routing and traffic-management target. No hidden deployment incident or backend topology is assumed.
CANDIDATES.INSTRUCTION_FIT: Approximately 8-11 concise grouped requirements can express the work package.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: A removed endpoint can remain reachable through the retry set.
A blocking drain implementation can prevent newer configuration from applying.
Idle keep-alive connections can outlive their endpoint.
Affinity can continue targeting a retired backend.
A health recovery event can accidentally re-admit an endpoint already marked for retirement.
Retired endpoint metrics can accumulate forever.
Unbounded drain semantics can strand long-lived streams indefinitely.
CANDIDATES.PERSONA: Edge deployment and reliability engineer responsible for disruption-free backend turnover.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: No new traffic is intentionally assigned to draining endpoints.
In-flight work has a bounded opportunity to finish.
Unchanged peers preserve their runtime routing state.
Transport resources do not leak across repeated turnover.
Planned membership transitions do not create a transient avoidable error spike.
REASONING_CHAIN: exclude draining targets from new selection and retries
allow bounded completion of existing work
REQUIRED_END_STATE: Endpoint identity remains stable across discovery updates.
New endpoints are admitted only after required readiness or health gates.
Active endpoints can transition into a draining state that excludes new traffic.
Affinity targeting a draining or failed endpoint is safely remapped.
Retries cannot select endpoints that are terminating or already failed for the request.
In-flight requests can complete within a bounded drain policy.
Long-lived streams have an explicit retirement deadline policy.
Retired endpoints release idle transport connections and runtime state.
Health transitions cannot accidentally reactivate a draining endpoint.
Per-endpoint telemetry is removed after retirement.

SCALE_FIT.F2P_SURFACE: Approximately 25-30 distinct lifecycle tests are plausible.
SCALE_FIT.P2P_SURFACE: Strong preservation coverage exists for unchanged peers, in-flight requests, connection cleanup, and ordinary routing.
SCALE_FIT.SUBSTANTIVE_RUNTIME_LOC: Approximately 4000 or more substantive LOC is plausible across lifecycle, selection, transport, reconciliation, and observability components.

outputs.WHY_THIS_ONE: GENERATION_SAFE_DYNAMIC_RECONCILIATION has the strongest strict-profile fit without padding. Its requirement families all participate in one causal architecture: a versioned runtime-state transition from validated input through reconciliation, state migration, atomic publication, request serving, retirement, checkpointing, and recovery. That coupling naturally supports at least 3000 substantive reachable LOC, approximately 20-30 distinct failure manifestations, approximately 25-30 non-duplicative functional tests, and meaningful preservation tests. It provides normal, edge, boundary, negative, concurrency, failure, and restart surfaces while remaining expressible in fewer than 20 concise material requirements. Public references establish that reload races, stale discovery state, load-balancer reset behavior, backend turnover, and stale telemetry are real engineering work shapes, but the candidate does not copy their prose or topology. No artificial data volume is needed because this is not naturally a data-backed workload.
